title: Strategy Profile
body_html:
Strategy Profile

For a strategic game $G=(I,(S_i)_{i\in I},(g_i)_{i\in I})$, a strategy profile is a simultaneous specification of one strategy for every player. It is an element $$ s=(s_i)_{i\in I}\in S:=\prod_{i\in I} S_i. $$ A profile is therefore not a strategy of one player; it is the full joint choice against which payoffs are evaluated. If player $i$'s component is $s_i$, then $g_i(s)$, also written $g_i(s_i,s_{-i})$, is player $i$'s payoff at the profile.

For a player $i$, the notation $s_{-i}$ denotes the subprofile of all players other than $i$, with strategy space $$ S_{-i}:=\prod_{j\ne i}S_j. $$ Thus the same profile may be written as $s=(s_i,s_{-i})$.

More generally, for a subset $J\subseteq I$, one writes $$ s_J=(s_j)_{j\in J}\in S_J:=\prod_{j\in J}S_j. $$ This notation lets later definitions compare $s$ with a unilateral replacement $(t_i,s_{-i})$, where only player $i$ changes strategy and every other component is kept fixed.

References

  • [MFoGT, Section 1.3.1] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. Profiles s = (s_i) and the notation s = (s_i,s_{-i}).
  • [MFoGT, Section 4.2] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. Product notation for S, S_J, and S_{-i}.
